topic: Demonstration and explanation on the operation of various elements of mechanics of an Altimeter, ASI, and VSI & Mach meter.
syllabus_extract: Demonstration and explanation on the operation of various elements of mechanics of an Altimeter, ASI, and VSI & Mach meter.
specific_objectives: 24.4.1 Trainee will be able to explain the operation of Altimeter, ASI, and VSI & Mach meter.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of instrument mechanics using cutaway models; Safety: Handle glass components with care; Supervision: Instructor monitors trainee interaction with models.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of an altimeter?
How does an Air Speed Indicator measure speed?
What is the relationship between vertical speed and pressure changes?

development.content:
Static pressure system operation
Altimeter case and capsule mechanics
Kollsman window adjustment function
Altitude setting and pressure reference
Error sources in altimeter readings

topics: ASI pitot tube and vent operation
Impact of airspeed on instrument accuracy
Relationship between indicated and true airspeed
development.content:
ASI pitot tube and vent operation
Diaphragm and Bourdon tube mechanics
Calibration and error correction
Impact of airspeed on instrument accuracy
Relationship between indicated and true airspeed

topics: VSI diaphragm and capillary tube action
Rate of climb and descent indication
Integration of Mach number with airspeed
development.content:
VSI diaphragm and capillary tube action
Rate of climb and descent indication
Mach meter operation and compressibility
Calibration of vertical speed indicators
Integration of Mach number with airspeed

summary_questions: Explain how the static port affects altimeter accuracy.
Describe the mechanical difference between an ASI and a VSI.
How does the Mach meter account for compressibility effects?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note comparing the static pressure usage in the Altimeter versus the ASI for the next lesson (LP 02).
